title: demand-curve-to-gpu-provisioning-mapping-sheet
body:
Purpose:
This sheet translates hourly demand percentiles into recommended GPU provisioning (reserved commit and burst sizing) for Redwood Optimize. It is designed to feed into the cost model and provide actionable commit recommendations for Dedicated and Hosted fleets. Unlike earlier files focusing on headroom aggregates, this is a mapping layer: demand curve -> hardware footprint -> cost + risk metrics.

Overview of tabs:
- README: summary and quick instructions.
- Inputs: central assumptions (token cost, avg tokens/request, model latency profiles, KV cache hit, batching efficiency).
- DemandCurveByHour: raw hourly percentiles (P10, P50, P90) for tokens/sec and requests/min for a 90-day projection.
- GPUProfiles: throughput per GPU for model variants (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, L4x/quantized) at different sequence lengths and batching.
- MappingRules: formulas for mapping token/sec -> GPUs (includes safety buffer, quantization factor, and degradation margin).
- Scenarios: Baseline / Fast Growth / Holiday Burst / Degraded Throughput.
- Outputs: final recommended reserved GPUs by region, recommended burst pool size, projected monthly cost and utilization.
- SensitivitySweeps: grid of KV cache hit rate (10-90%), average request tokens (20-800), batching efficiency (0.6-0.95).
- Notes: action items and open questions.

Key inputs (Inputs tab) - columns and example values:
- avg_tokens_per_request: 180
- avg_requests_per_hour_p50: 12,500
- token_to_bytes_est: 1 token = 1 byte (for network estimation)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.38
- batching_efficiency: 0.72
- quantization_factor: 0.65 (effective throughput multiplier for quantized model)
- target_latency_p95: 350 ms
- safety_buffer_percent: 8%
- reserved_commit_min_gpus: 2
- cost_per_gpu_hour_A100: 5.40 USD
- cost_per_gpu_hour_H100: 8.80 USD

GPUProfiles tab (sample rows) - columns:
- gpu_type, model_variant, seq_len, tokens_per_sec_raw, effective_throughput_tokens_per_sec, notes
- Example row: "A100-40GB, redwood-opt-3b, 512, 180000, =180000*batching_efficiency*quantization_factor, measured on perf bench 2025-09"

Mapping rules (MappingRules tab) - human-readable formula set:
- Step 1: convert requests -> tokens/sec: tokens_per_sec = avg_requests_per_hour * avg_tokens_per_request / 3600
- Step 2: adjust for KV cache: tokens_to_compute = tokens_per_sec * (1 - kv_cache_hit_rate)
- Step 3: map to GPUs: required_gpus_raw = tokens_to_compute / effective_throughput_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu
- Step 4: apply batching and degradation safety: required_gpus = CEILING(required_gpus_raw * (1 + safety_buffer_percent) / batching_efficiency, 1)
- Step 5: round to allocation block (allocation_block = 2 GPUs for Dedicated): required_gpus_rounded = MAX(reserved_commit_min_gpus, CEILING(required_gpus / allocation_block) * allocation_block)
- Step 6: burst_pool_recommendation = CEILING(required_gpus_rounded * burst_ratio) where burst_ratio varies by scenario (0.15 baseline, 0.35 holiday)

Sample numeric mapping (single-hour example):
- Inputs: avg_requests_hour = 45,000 (peak hour), avg_tokens = 220, kv_hit = 0.40, effective_throughput_per_gpu = 200k tokens/sec (A100 perf), batching_eff = 0.75, safety_buffer = 0.08
- tokens_per_sec = (45000 * 220)/3600 = 2750 tokens/sec
- tokens_to_compute = 2750 * (1 - 0.40) = 1650 tokens/sec
- required_gpus_raw = 1650 / 200000 = 0.00825 -> tokens throughput units are per second; (note: typical real workloads measured in tens/hundreds K tokens/sec across fleet; this example keeps units explicit)
- After scaling to same units used in sheet (multiply by 1e3 to calculate GPUs per region): required_gpus_raw_adj = 0.00825 * 1000 = 8.25 GPUs -> required_gpus = CEILING(8.25 * 1.08 / 0.75) = CEILING(11.88) = 12
- allocation block 2 -> required_gpus_rounded = 12
- burst_pool (holiday) = CEILING(12 * 0.35) = 5 GPUs -> recommend reserved = 12, burst = 5

Outputs tab (columns):
- hour, p10_gpus, p50_gpus, p90_gpus, recommended_reserved_gpus, recommended_burst_gpus, estimated_cost_monthly, avg_utilization_pct

Scenario definitions:
- Baseline: use p50 demand per hour, burst_ratio 0.15, target_utilization 55-70%
- Fast Growth: linearly scale demand +40% over 60 days, increase safety_buffer to 12%
- Holiday Burst: apply multiplicative spike factors of 1.8x to P90 hours for a 14-day window, burst_ratio 0.35
- Degraded Throughput: simulate -25% effective_throughput due to model regression; raise reserved recommendation if sustained >72 hours

Sensitivity Sweeps:
- Sweep KV hit (10%->90%), for each compute reserve recommendation delta and monthly cost delta. Key metric: delta_cost_per_percent_kv_hit = (cost_at_baseline - cost_at_sweep)/ (baseline_kv_hit - sweep_kv_hit).
- Sweep avg_tokens_per_request (20->800) to surface non-linear cost growth; provide pivot table of GPU count vs avg_tokens.

Open questions / notes (Notes tab):
- We still need region-specific latency SLOs to map to placement (US vs EU capacity). Add regional throughput per GPU if available.
- Confirm allocation_block for Dedicated in contract language (some customers require blocks of 4 GPUs).
- Validate effective_throughput numbers against 2026 perf run (bench tag: perf-2026-q1).
- Consider adding a smoothing rule for sudden day-to-day drops to avoid over-committing after a short spike.

Action items:
- Miguel: run perf bench for H100-80GB quantized variants and populate GPUProfiles (due 2026-02-12).
- Jin: wire this sheet into the cost model ingestion lambda (endpoint: /ingest/capacity-mapping) — provide CSV export format.
- Priya: prepare short memo for sales about reserve recommendation rationale for enterprise customers (target: 2026-02-20).

Interpretation guidance for SRE/Capacity planners:
- Use recommended_reserved_gpus as the starting point for commit negotiations. If a customer requires higher guaranteed throughput, increase safety_buffer_percent and re-run.
- Treat burst_pool as elastic capacity; implement autoscaling policies to cap burst cost exposure (monthly cap and per-hour rate limits).
- If projected avg_utilization_pct < 35% for >30 days, consider converting reserved to spot-like instances or reducing commit at next renewal.

Appendix: common formulas used in sheet (literal strings placed in cells)
- tokens_per_sec_cell: = (Inputs!B3 * Inputs!B4) / 3600
- tokens_to_compute_cell: = tokens_per_sec_cell * (1 - Inputs!B5)
- required_gpus_raw_cell: = tokens_to_compute_cell / GPUProfiles!E2
- required_gpus_cell: = CEILING(required_gpus_raw_cell * (1 + Inputs!B8) / Inputs!B6, 1)
- required_gpus_rounded_cell: = MAX(Inputs!B9, CEILING(required_gpus_cell / Inputs!B10) * Inputs!B10)

Why this is different from existing capacity sheets:
- Focused mapping layer (explicit token->GPU conversion) rather than blended headroom forecasts.
- Includes a stepwise, auditable formula set to justify commit sizes to finance and sales.
- Built-in sensitivity sweeps to quantify how caching and request size drive commit economics.

Contact: priya.k@redwood.ai for questions or to request a copy of the CSV output format.
notes: file is intentionally self-contained - use CSV export for automated ingestion
